messages:
sam: FYI new onboarding ticket for Aquifer. They're seeing a burst of 429s during ephemeral key rotation. Sharing debug trace and their init pattern.
sam: trace excerpt:
```
2026-03-22T09:14:01Z WARN   preflight validate status=429 path=/v1/preflight/validate retry-after=1
2026-03-22T09:14:01Z ERROR  request failed status=429 path=/v1/chat/completions client_id=aquifer-12
2026-03-22T09:14:02Z WARN   token refresh concurrent=72 origin=ec2-54-23-12-45.eu-west-1.compute.amazonaws.com
```
sam: Their onboarding script spawns 70 worker processes that call our Node SDK client.init() all at once after a CI secret rotate. They're on node-sdk v1.3.0.
tara: do we know whether they call the token exchange or fetch ephemeral directly from our API?
sam: they call our /tokens/ephemeral directly from the browser via a lightweight serverless function. No server-side coalesce.
andrew: alerts-bot just posted an anomaly: :alerts-bot:
alerts-bot: [alert] rate_limit_burst account=aquifer region=eu-west window=00:00:10 peak_rps=210 baseline_rps=20 id=rl-20260322-77
andrew: classic rotate stampede. Quick playbook items: 1) ask them to gate init calls behind a single server-side exchange so browsers don't all hit us; 2) apply client-side randomized backoff with capped concurrency; 3) we can temporarily open a 90s elevated priority window to let inflight succeed while they patch.
tara: I'll take customer comms and request their init snippet + which infra (workers vs browser). sam can you attach their serverless function code?
sam: pasted their snippet:
```js
// spawn 70 child processes in CI that each do:
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.EPH_KEY })
await client.chat.create({ model: 'redwood-lite', messages: [...] })
```
sam: they rely on the client to fetch ephemeral directly from our /tokens endpoint in the browser.
andrew: infra notes: enable short-term preflight coalescing for account=aquifer when concurrent preflight > 50 within 15s. That should dedupe identical /tokens/ephemeral calls. Add a soft allowlist for the next 2 minutes.
andrew: Also toggle edge keep-alive pooling and avoid creating new TLS sessions per init. That reduced impact for a previous customer.
tara: sent to Aquifer: "We see a short-lived surge at rotation. Please adopt server-side token exchange or reduce browser concurrency; deploy a tiny backoff wrapper in your init flow. We'll lift a temporary priority window for 90s to drain pending requests. See attached suggested patch."
tara: suggested client patch (sent):
```js
// lightweight concurrency cap + jitter
const MAX_CONC = 8
const queue = []
async function gatedInit() {
  while (getActive() >= MAX_CONC) await sleep(Math.random()*200 + 50)
  try { return await client.init() }
  catch (e) { if (e.status===429) await sleep((Math.random()*500)+100); throw e }
}
```
sam: customer replied: "we can change browser flow, but our product team wants to keep direct ephemeral fetch in clients for fast startup. Can you recommend a server-side proxy pattern?"
andrew: recommend a lightweight token broker: single server endpoint that exchanges long-lived key for ephemeral and caches identical requests for 2s. If multiple clients ask for token for same user within that window, broker returns same ephemeral. That removes fanout.
tara: I've authorized the 90s priority window, CS notes: case# 55231. I'll post follow-up with guidance docs and a renewal note summarizing recommended rotation strategy.
sam: after applying temporary coalesce and customer deploying concurrency cap, their 429 rate dropped by ~92% in 2 minutes. They asked for a one-paragraph blurb for their renewal pack about "recommended rotation best practices."
andrew: I'll file infra change rl-20260322-77:coalesce enabled for account=aquifer window=90s. Add a followup task to infra backlog to consider global lightweight broker for ephemeral-heavy customers.
tara: drafting the renewal blurb now and will upload to the account playbook. closing this thread after 24h of stability. :thumbsup:
